interaction.$description: Default-state background fill for the primary (main accent/CTA) control — the base color a control uses to signal "this is the main action" before any hover/active/selected/disabled state is applied.

error.$description: Background fill for a control communicating an error or destructive state (e.g. a destructive/delete button, or a control flagged invalid) — the fill color a control uses to signal "this represents an error or a destructive action."

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: surface background color, non-interactive background, default/neutral control fill

base.$description: Neutral background for a container component that accepts child content — the `base` value on the concept axis (see docs/glossary.yaml's `base` entry): no specific color role applied, same as `bg.fill.base`/`text.base` would be for their own elements. Also the un-elevated (ground-level) surface — an elevated container (Card, Popover, etc.) should use the future `raised` token once one exists, not this one.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: control fill, interactive/pressable background, error surface variant, an elevated/raised container surface

raised.$description: Background for a container component that sits above the page's `base` surface (e.g. Card, Popover) — the `raised` elevation value (see docs/glossary.yaml's `raised` entry), orthogonal to the concept axis: a raised surface can still carry `base`, or in principle any other concept, on top of it.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: control fill, the page-level/ground surface (use bg-surface-base for that), error surface variant

error.$description: Background for a container component when it is communicating an error state (e.g. an inline error panel, an invalid form section, an alert container) — the surface color a container uses to signal "this content represents an error."

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: control fill, default/neutral surface, non-error alert surfaces

base.$description: Base body text color — the `base` value on the concept axis (see docs/glossary.yaml's `base` entry): no specific color role applied, used wherever no more specific semantic text role (primary, error, on-fill, etc.) applies.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: text placed on top of a fill background (use an on-fill variant instead), emphasized/primary text, error text

primary.$description: Text rendered in the primary (main accent/CTA) color role — e.g. a link, an emphasized label, or text calling attention using the accent color — set on a surface background, not on top of a filled control.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: text on top of a bg-fill-primary/interaction background (use text-on-fill-primary instead), base/neutral body text, error text

on-fill-primary.$description: Text/icon color for content placed directly on top of a bg-fill-interaction (primary) background — e.g. label text inside a primary/filled button — contrast-verified against that fill.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: text on a surface/base background, text on any other fill color (error, etc.), text-primary's own surface-background use case

error.$description: Text color for content communicating an error (e.g. a validation message, an inline error label) — set on a surface/base background, not on top of a filled control.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: text on top of a bg-fill-error background (use text-on-fill-error instead), base/neutral text

on-fill-error.$description: Text/icon color for content placed directly on top of a bg-fill-error background — e.g. label text inside a destructive/error-filled button — contrast-verified against that fill.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: text on a surface/base background, text on any other fill color, text-error's own surface-background use case

control.$description: Default border color for atomic control components (e.g. Input, Checkbox, Select) — the border a control uses in its neutral/default state. Note: `control` here is a plain-English description in the `concept` slot (border has no `family` segment), not a value on the surface/fill classification axis — see the glossary's "container / control" entry.

com.eldrin-ui.intent.notFor: container/surface borders, error/focus border variants, divider lines
